name: Home laser hair removal

lead: Home laser hair removal devices use a low-energy diode laser to reduce hair growth, similar in principle to IPL but with a narrow wavelength. One cleared device was tested in a small trial showing sustained reductions one year after treatment.
The same caveats as IPL apply: suitable mainly for dark hair on lighter skin, and results rest on small, often manufacturer-linked studies.

paras: Pigment in the hair absorbs the laser light and heats the follicle, damaging it to slow regrowth. Low energy per pulse means weekly or monthly sessions over months.

Burns, pigment change and eye injury are possible, especially on darker skin or with misuse. The best study (Wheeland 2012) had 13 participants and author ties to the maker, and comparisons show home devices do less than professional lasers. Long-term data are limited.
